name: safe-feed-fetch
summary: Fetch a user-supplied feed, chapters or transcript URL on a server without opening an SSRF hole: every redirect hop re-checked, every resolved address checked, private and special-use IPv4 and IPv6 refused, and the body read under a byte cap.

fixes: Added IPv6 multicast ff00::/8 to PRIVATE_V6, which the site's list does not have. A connect to a multicast address fails anyway, so this makes the refusal explicit; it closes no reachable hole. ITDV-Lightning carries the same refusal in its own wrapper (lib/proxy-guard.ts at 8b7fa61) because its copy of this file is byte-identical to the site's.

peer.runtime: safe-fetch.ts: Node 18+ server only (node:dns/promises). capped-body.ts: any runtime, browser included - it imports nothing.

caveats: Residual risk, stated in the file itself: this is resolve-then-fetch, so a DNS server that answers the check with a public address and the connection with a private one (classic rebinding) still gets through. Closing it needs a dialer that pins the checked address.
The port is not restricted. A public host is reachable on any port, 22 included.
Plain http is allowed on purpose: a long tail of real podcast feeds is still http.
safeFetch sets no timeout and no User-Agent. Pass both: safeFetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(8000), headers: { 'User-Agent': 'your-app/1.0' } }).
safeFetch does not read the body. Read it with readCappedText(res) (8 MB default) or readCappedJson(res); never res.text(), which has no limit.
The thrown errors name the host. Map them to a generic 4xx before you answer a client.

Any redirect and next option you pass is overridden: redirects are always followed by hand, and cache is always no-store. Do not remove the override: on a cacheable fetch Next reads a copy of the whole body to store it, outside the 8 MB cap.

Next.js: because the fetch is no-store, a route or page with export const revalidate silently becomes dynamic (the build passes, every request fetches again), and a catch around safeFetch receives Next's 'Dynamic server usage' error during the build - retrying it can push the prerender past Next's 60 s limit and fail the build. Call unstable_rethrow(err) first in such a catch. To keep a cache, wrap the fetch, capped read and parse in unstable_cache (the route stays static and only your returned data is cached; tested on Next 15.5.28), or set dynamic = 'force-dynamic' and send a CDN Cache-Control (s-maxage). See the README section 'Next.js: this fetch turns revalidate off'.
